subject.title: Memory MVP: build write pipeline with classification, dedupe, merge, and conflict handling

question: Should the Memory MVP write resolver be owned by memory-core as the active-memory contract, by Memory Wiki as the knowledge-layer workflow, or by a new plugin/SDK seam before implementation starts?
rationale: The missing behavior is clear, but the issue defines durable memory schema, conflict policy, provenance semantics, and operator UX, which automation cannot safely choose from code alone.

options.title: Design active-memory contract first
options.body: Use memory-core or a narrow active-memory SDK contract as the owner for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history, with Memory Wiki consuming or mirroring the settled provenance model.

options.title: Route through Memory Wiki
options.body: Treat contradictions, claims, evidence, and source freshness as Memory Wiki responsibilities while keeping memory-core focused on Markdown recall, promotion, and dreaming until a lower-level write API is needed.

options.title: Defer the MVP resolver
options.body: Keep the current Markdown, promotion, LanceDB, and wiki layers while gathering more production examples before accepting durable schema or UX commitments.

recommendation.title: Design active-memory contract first
recommendation.body: Use memory-core or a narrow active-memory SDK contract as the owner for candidate classification, source-required resolution, conflict state, and revision history, with Memory Wiki consuming or mirroring the settled provenance model.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter has the strongest sampled history on the memory host/plugin ownership boundary where this product decision needs to land.
